title: withdrawRewardToken authorisation widened from plan-specified onlyOwner to onlyOwnerOrMigrator
description: The migration plan ('NFTStakerV2 deltas' section, code block on line 188) explicitly specifies `withdrawRewardToken(address to, uint256 amount) external onlyOwner`. The implementation widens access to `onlyOwnerOrMigrator` (line 564), allowing the migrator address to drain the contract's full phUSD balance to an arbitrary recipient `to` once `totalStaked == 0 && paused()` hold. The migrator role is owner-set via `setMigrator` (line 244) but is not described anywhere in the plan — the plan models the helper as a stateless, single-purpose contract calling `stakeFor`. Per the plan's MigrationHelper section, the helper has 'no admin, no upgrade path. Holds no funds between txs.' Granting it (or any future migrator) drain rights is a deviation from the documented authorisation surface. The drain magnitude is bounded only by the contract balance: at the documented runway (~910 phUSD carried over + new mint sized to match), this is on the order of thousands of phUSD per single migrator-signed call.
impact: Trust surface for the entire phUSD reward budget widens from the owner key (per plan) to {owner, migrator}. If the migrator is ever a contract with weaker key custody, a privileged-helper bug, or is later repurposed without revoking, all phUSD in the staker can be diverted to an arbitrary address. The constraint that `totalStaked == 0 && paused()` must hold gates the window but does not gate the magnitude. Note: pure centralisation findings are out of scope, but this is specifically a documented onlyOwner -> implemented onlyOwnerOrMigrator deviation, not a generic admin power.
recommendation: Either (a) revert to plan-spec `onlyOwner` on `withdrawRewardToken` and remove the `onlyOwnerOrMigrator` path, or (b) update the migration plan to explicitly grant the migrator role drain access, document the operational rationale, and consider scoping the migrator's allowed `to` (e.g. only `owner()` recipient) so the migrator can trigger the sweep but cannot redirect funds.
attack_scenario:
1. Owner deploys NFTStakerV2, funds it with the runway-matching phUSD mint per step 11 of the plan.
2. Owner sets migrator = MigrationHelper per step 9.
3. (Later) A future incident requires rotating the helper. Owner calls `setMigrator(newHelper)`. If `newHelper` is buggy or compromised in a future deployment, or if any future migrator role-holder is a multisig/EOA with weaker custody than the staker owner, that party can:
   a. Wait for a moment when totalStaked == 0 (e.g. after the migration window closes per plan step 13, or after a future mass-unstake event).
   b. Request pauser to pause (or wait for a routine pause), or call `pause()` if migrator is also pauser.
   c. Call `withdrawRewardToken(attackerAddress, fullBalance)` — drains all phUSD to attackerAddress.
4. Alternative path: the migrator itself can call `unstakeFor(beneficiary, all)` repeatedly to drive totalStaked to 0 (NFTs land at the migrator per line 558), then trigger the drain. The pause gate still applies, but the migrator only needs one cooperative pause to complete the sequence.
